title: Digital or Print? How Do You Read Books?
main_content:
A South African technology expert says huge numbers of book readers in his country are using electronic reading devices. He says the rising popularity of such devices, known as e-readers, could lead to the slow disappearance of traditional books.

Our story begins at a bookstore in the city of Johannesburg. Many people like to look through a book before buying it. But how much longer will traditional bookstores continue operating?

Arthur Goldstuck studies technological developments in Africa for World Wide Worx, a company based in Johannesburg. He says electronic books are growing in popularity and threatening the future of bookstores.

Mr. Goldstuck says his brain tells him electronic books are the future of reading in South Africa. But his heart tells him there will always be a place in the country for printed books.

The number of electronic reading devices in South Africa is growing. But so is the number of stores selling second-hand, used books. Mr. Goldstuck says this is happening because new books are overpriced in South Africa.

Doron Locketz (Book Dealers store owner) says the printed book will survive e-books because South Africans like “face-to-face” service from booksellers.

But he warns that unless booksellers tell young people about the many reasons for owning printed books, their stores will not survive.

questions.question: What can the rising popularity of e-readers lead to?
options: The slow disappearance of traditional books
questions.answer: The slow disappearance of traditional books

questions.question: What does Mr. Goldstuck’s heart tell him?
options: There will always be a demand for electronic books
Printed books will continue to have a place in South Africa
All bookstores will inevitably close down
E-books will completely replace printed materials
questions.answer: Printed books will continue to have a place in South Africa

questions.question: The number of e-readers in South Africa is growing. But what else is growing?
options: The number of stores selling second-hand, used books
questions.answer: The number of stores selling second-hand, used books
